extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners preparing or reviewing patent application drawings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and requirements for preparing and submitting drawings, photographs, and graphical material in U.S. utility, design, plant, and reissue patent applications under 37 CFR 1.84 and related MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable drawing media (black ink vs. color)
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required; India ink or its equivalent that secures solid black lines must be used. Color drawings are permitted only in rare circumstances where color is the only practical medium to disclose the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings must be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible in black and white in the printed patent; color drawings are not permitted in international (PCT) applications or in applications (or copies) submitted under the Office electronic filing system; acceptance of color drawings requires a petition under 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2) including the fee (§1.17(h)), three sets of color drawings, and an amendment inserting specified language in the brief description of the drawings. Examiners must object to color drawings until a petition is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs — when black and white photos are allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs (including photocopies) are not ordinarily permitted but will be accepted if they are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention (e.g., electrophoresis gels, blots, autoradiographs, cell cultures, histological sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, thin layer chromatography plates, crystalline structures, and ornamental effects in design applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must be of sufficient quality that all details are reproducible in the printed patent; if the subject admits illustration by drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead. Black and white photographs submitted in lieu of ink drawings must comply with 37 CFR 1.84(b) and no petition/fee is required for black and white photographs; only one set of photographs is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Color photographs will be accepted only if the conditions for accepting color drawings and black and white photographs have been satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat color photographs like color drawings: petition with fee, three sets of color photographs, amendment with required brief-description language, and the petition is decided by a Supervisory Patent Examiner. IFW applications may maintain color photographs in an artifact folder. Filing color in a continuing application requires renewal of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia should be provided on drawings and, if provided, should include the title of the invention, inventor’s name, and application number or docket number placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each drawing sheet submitted after filing must be identified as either "Replacement Sheet" or "New Sheet" pursuant to §1.121(d). Marked-up copies of amended drawing figures with annotations must be clearly labeled "Annotated Sheet" per §1.121(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms may be submitted as drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements as drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure (using brackets when necessary) to show proper integration. Each group of waveforms must be presented as a single figure with a common vertical axis and time along the horizontal axis; each individual waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type and condition of paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing sheets must be on paper that is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable; all sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, folds, erasures, alterations, overwritings, and interlineations; only one side of the sheet may be used for the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must be developed on paper meeting the sheet-size and margin requirements of paragraphs (f) and (g). Good quality copies from office copiers are acceptable if lines are uniformly thick, black, and solid. Facsimile copies acceptable under limited conditions but ensure transmission does not degrade quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size of drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size; one of the shorter sides is regarded as the top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted sizes: 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (DIN A4) or 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches). Consistent sheet size is required for ease of handling and reproduction; see MPEP §608.01 for treatment when filing-as-filed does not meet sheet size/margin requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and sight area
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets must not contain frames around the sight and should have scan target points (cross-hairs) printed on two cater-corner margin corners. Required margins: top ≥2.5 cm (1 inch), left ≥2.5 cm (1 inch), right ≥1.5 cm (5/8 inch), bottom ≥1.0 cm (3/8 inch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These margins leave a maximum sight area (usable surface) no greater than specified for each sheet size. Numbers and identification placed in the top margin must follow placement rules. For certified copies that do not meet margin/size requirements, see MPEP §608.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views — number, type, grouping, and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing must contain as many views as necessary to show the invention; views may be plan, elevation, section, or perspective; detail views on larger scale may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All views must be grouped together and arranged on the sheet(s) without wasting space, preferably upright, clearly separated from one another, and must not be included on sheets containing the specification, claims, or abstract. Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines (except as specified); waveforms may be connected by dashed lines to show relative timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploded views
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploded views with separated parts embraced by a bracket to show relationship/order of assembly are permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an exploded view appears on the same sheet as another figure, it should be placed in brackets. Follow spacing and grouping rules to avoid crowding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial views and linking across sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: A large machine or device may be shown as partial views on a single sheet or extended over several sheets provided there is no loss in comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial views on separate sheets must be capable of being linked edge-to-edge so that no partial view contains parts of another partial view. Include a smaller scale view showing the whole formed by the partial views and indicating positions of the parts shown. Enlarged portions and their originals must be labeled as separate views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional views and hatching
rubrics_metrics.description: The plane upon which a sectional view is taken should be indicated on the view from which the section is cut by a broken line designated by numerals corresponding to the sectional view; arrows indicate the direction of sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hatching must be used to indicate sectioned portions with regularly spaced oblique parallel lines distinguishable without difficulty, preferably at 45°. Hatching should not impede reference characters or lead lines; may be broken off where reference characters are inserted. A cross section must show all materials as they appear in the view; juxtaposed different elements must be hatched in different ways. For large areas, hatching may be confined to an edging. Different hatching types should have conventional meanings where material is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate positions and modified forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Moved or alternate positions may be shown by a broken line superimposed on a suitable view if not crowded; otherwise a separate view must be used. Modified forms of construction must be shown in separate views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use separate views when necessary to avoid crowding; label and arrange modified forms to be clearly distinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and orientation of views and text
rubrics_metrics.description: One view must not be placed upon or within the outline of another; all views on the same sheet should stand in the same direction and preferably so readable with the sheet held upright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If views wider than the sheet are necessary, the sheet may be turned on its side so the top (heading space) is on the right-hand side. Words must appear horizontally left-to-right when the page is upright or turned so that the top becomes the right side, except for graphs using standard scientific conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view selection
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the views should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may suggest a single view by figure number for inclusion on the front page. Views for front page must comply with the rules (not connected by projection lines, no center lines, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The scale of a drawing must be large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when the drawing is reduced in size to two-thirds in reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications such as "actual size" or "scale 1/2" are not permitted since these lose meaning with reproduction in different formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings must be made by a process giving satisfactory reproduction characteristics. Every line, number, and letter must be durable, clean, black (except color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line and letter weight must permit adequate reproduction; this applies to very fine lines, shading, and cut-surface lines. Different line thicknesses may be used where they have different meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading is encouraged if it aids understanding and does not reduce legibility; used to indicate surface or shape of spherical, cylindrical, and conical elements; flat parts may be lightly shaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer spaced thin lines, as few as practicable, contrasting with the rest of the drawing. Heavy lines on the shade side may substitute for shading except where they overlap or obscure reference characters. Light should come from the upper left at 45°. Solid black shading areas are not permitted except for bar graphs or color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols and legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements where appropriate and must be adequately identified in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Known devices should use universally recognized conventional symbols; other symbols not universally recognized may be used subject to Office approval if not likely to be confused with conventional symbols and readily identifiable. ANSI publications are acceptable guides but the Office will not approve a published collection of symbols as a group; avoid overly specific/unclear symbols and label nonstandard symbols. Legends should contain as few words as possible and may be required by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters — form, size, and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (numerals preferred), sheet numbers, and view numbers must be plain, legible, not enclosed in brackets or circles, and oriented in the same direction as the view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange reference characters to follow the profile of the object. Use the English alphabet for letters except where customarily another alphabet is used. Numbers, letters, and reference characters must measure at least 0.32 cm (1/8 inch) in height and should not interfere with comprehension or be placed on hatched/shaded surfaces. The same part appearing in more than one view must always have the same reference character and the same reference character must never designate different parts. Reference characters mentioned in the description must appear in the drawings; characters not mentioned in the description shall not appear in the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines are the lines between reference characters and the details referred to; they may be straight or curved and should be as short as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead lines must originate in the immediate proximity of the reference character and extend to the feature indicated; they must not cross each other. Lead lines are required for each reference character except those indicating the surface or cross section on which they are placed (these characters must be underlined). Lead lines must be executed in the same manner as other drawing lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views and single-view rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1, independent of sheet numbering, and in the order they appear if possible. Partial views forming one complete view must use the same number followed by a capital letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View numbers must be preceded by the abbreviation "FIG.". If only a single view is used in an application to illustrate the claimed invention, it must not be numbered and "FIG." must not appear. Numbers/letters identifying the views must be simple, clear, not enclosed, and larger than numbers used for reference characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings and corrections permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on the drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin. Corrections on drawings must be durable and permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No holes should be made by applicant in the drawing sheets. Corrections submitted to the Office should be in the form of replacement sheets labeled "Replacement Sheet" since the Office does not release drawings for correction; see 37 CFR 1.85 and MPEP §608.02(p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows usage and meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at the ends of lines provided their meaning is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a freestanding arrow on a lead line to indicate an entire section towards which it points; an arrow touching a line to indicate the surface shown by the line looking along the arrow's direction; or arrows to show direction of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or mask work notice placement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing but must be placed within the sight immediately below the figure representing the copyrighted or mask work material and limited to letters 0.32 to 0.64 cm (1/8 to 1/4 inches) high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content must be limited to legally provided elements (e.g., "©1983 John Doe" or "*M* John Doe"). Inclusion is permitted only if the authorization language of §1.71(e) is included at the beginning of the specification (preferably first paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1 within the sight as defined in paragraph (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheet numbers, if present, must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet (but not in the margin) or on the right-hand side if the drawing extends too close to the middle. Numbering must be clear and larger than reference characters. The number of each sheet should be shown by two Arabic numerals on either side of an oblique line (sheet number/total number of sheets) with no other marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable physical/electronic copy practices and reproduction concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings on paper are acceptable if in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84; good quality office copier copies acceptable if uniformly thick, black, and solid. Facsimile copies acceptable when mailed/hand-carried or submitted with issue fee payment under stated procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure facsimile/transmission does not unreasonably degrade drawing quality. Drawings are accepted in two different size formats but all sheets in an application must be the same size. For prints, preparation/distribution/return, see MPEP §508 and §608.02(m)/(y). For amendment of drawings, see MPEP §714.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of drawing types (original, substitute, acceptable, informal, corrected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms defined include Original drawings (submitted with application when filed), Substitute drawing (filed later to replace an original informal drawing), Acceptable drawing (acceptable for publication or issuance), Informal drawing (does not comply with form requirements of 37 CFR 1.84), Corrected drawing (includes corrections of informalities and examiner-approved changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal drawings may be acceptable for publication/examination; an objection will generally be made only if the Office cannot reproduce the drawing or the contents are unacceptable to the examiner. Drawing prints and interference prints are specific internal copies used by OPAP/IFW with particular handling and placement instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph preparation standards and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs or photomicrographs printed on sensitized double-weight smooth white paper are acceptable as final drawings in lieu of India ink drawings for inventions incapable of accurate depiction by ink drawings (e.g., gels, microstructures, textiles, ornamental effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must show the invention more clearly than ink drawings and comply with drawing rules. Photographs filed on/after Oct 1, 2001 may not be mounted on Bristol Board. If several photographs form one sheet, they must be developed on a single sheet. Photographs in IFW applications may be treated as artifacts maintained in an artifact folder if scanning cannot reproduce them accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings — administrative considerations and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited use of color drawings in utility patent applications is provided under 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2); color drawings and color photographs will not be accepted unless a petition is filed and granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include the fee (§1.17(h)), three sets of color drawings/photographs, and an amendment inserting required brief-description language. The petition is decided by a Supervisory Patent Examiner; until granted, the examiner must object to color submissions. Color submissions in continuing applications require renewal of the petition. Because printing patents in color imposes administrative/economic burden, issued patent copies depict drawings in black & white; color sets will be attached to Letters Patent and color copies provided upon request and payment to recover actual costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP review and correction timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings in utility and plant applications will be reviewed by the Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) for compliance with certain requirements of 37 CFR 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will send a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers if drawings are not acceptable for publication, giving applicant 2 months from mailing to file acceptable drawings (extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a)). OPAP will not release applications to the Technology Centers until acceptable drawings are filed.
